      <p>Held at the American Museum of Natural History in New York, the 2025 meeting was the first in-person OpenSpace user gathering. Planetarium directors, museum educators, university researchers, and the OpenSpace development team spent two days on demos, workshops, and conversation about where the software is heading.</p>

<!-- ── Sessions ────────────────────────────────────────────── -->
<section class="ds-venue-section ds-venue-section--alt" id="sessions">

    <div class="um-detail-body">
      <p>The program included development team previews of upcoming features, hands-on workshops for dome operators integrating OpenSpace with existing systems, lightning talks from users showcasing novel implementations, and open discussion sessions on community priorities.</p>
      <p>A few session highlights:</p>
      <ul>
        <li>New space-weather visualization workflows from NASA&rsquo;s Community Coordinated Modelling Center</li>
        <li>Live demonstration of the latest mission visualization profiles</li>
        <li>Hands-on dome integration troubleshooting with the development team</li>
        <li>Lightning talks from users at six institutions on novel implementations</li>
      </ul>
